name: Anthony Chabot Campground
coord_source: ReserveAmerica's Anthony Chabot Regional Park overview page, read 2026-09-16. PARK PRECISION: the pair is on the park overview, and this park holds eight campgrounds -- the family campground and seven group camps scattered across it. The point answers 'how far is this park from home'; it does not navigate to a pitch.
reservation_method: Park office (not reservations): (510) 690-6676, or 888-327-2757 option 3 ext. 4502
nightly_entry_cutoff: 10:00 PM, and it is a lock-out rather than a courtesy: entry gates are locked every night at 10pm and NO entry is possible until they re-open at 8am the next morning. Campers may EXIT at any time, so a late departure is fine and a late arrival is not. Stated by EBRPD, unlike Del Valle's cutoff, which this project holds only as a visitor's near-miss report.
fee_notes: Per night: tent or RV site with no hook-ups $35; RV site with water, sewer and 30-amp electrical $45; tent only, hike-in $25. RESERVATION FEE $8 PER SITE on top of the nightly rate. RV sewage disposal $20/use. Limited overflow parking $8/night/vehicle. Firewood $10/bundle and charcoal $15/bag at the campground kiosk -- but there is NO CAMP STORE, so bring everything else. Accepts cash, Visa, MasterCard and Discover. Fees subject to change.
notes: THE SITE COUNT RESOLVES, AND THE PAGE'S OWN LIST IS WRONG. 12 RV + 53 drive-up tent + 10 hike-in is exactly 75, so the '1 developed group site' the prose lists inside those 75 does not belong there: Puma Point is real, but it is a separate unit, not one of the 75 individual campsites. An earlier note here recorded the list as summing to 76 while calling itself 75; this is why. BEWARE A COINCIDENCE: the booking system's 'ALL 76' is NOT that same 76. It counts 69 individually listed sites plus 7 group camps, while the prose's faulty list counts 75 individual sites plus Puma Point. Two different quantities that happen to match. ONLY 69 OF THE 75 INDIVIDUAL SITES APPEAR ONLINE. Sites 010, 031, 033, 039, 053 and 075 are absent from the booking system's list entirely, so browsing online does not show the full inventory and a party counting availability there is counting 69. WHY THEY ARE ABSENT IS NOT STATED. The likeliest reading is that they are the accessible sites -- the same booking system says ADA campsites must be reserved by phone only, and the brochure confirms disabled accessible sites exist here -- but no source read says so, and they could equally be closed or out of service. Treated as a hypothesis, not a fact; ask Reservations. LOOPS, which the booking system names and no other source does: Loop A sites 1-12, the RV sites with 30-amp full hookups (11 listed, 010 absent); Loop B sites 13-22, 'Hike-In Sites (NO driving to site)', all 10 listed; Loop C sites 23-33, tent, 9 listed; Loop D sites 34-61, tent, 26 listed; Loop F sites 62-75, tent, 13 listed. There is no Loop E. PETS ARE ALLOWED AT EVERY SITE without exception -- all 76 listings, group camps and hike-in sites included, carry the Pets Allowed marker. THE OPEN SEASON IS UNCONFIRMED AND IT IS THE FACT MOST LIKELY TO COST A TRIP. The booking system says SEASONALLY CLOSED 1 NOVEMBER - 1 APRIL, with select sites closed through May. THE PARK BROCHURE CONTRADICTS THAT, saying year-round camping is available; see the open conflict, and treat the closure as live until it is settled, because acting on 'year-round' costs the trip rather than an argument. 75 campsites: 53 drive-up tent, 10 hike-in tent (#13-22) and 12 RV with full hookups (30 amp), plus Puma Point, a developed group site inside the campground with its own row -- the page's own list sums to 76 while calling itself 75. THE HIKE-IN SITES ARE NOT BACKPACK SITES: they sit inside the campground 0.2 miles (about 1,000 feet) from parking with no vehicle access, EBRPD suggests bringing a wagon, and they are priced at the $25 tent-only rate. NO RIGS OVER 35 FEET, stated twice by the booking system and matching the brochure; the campground page's 'pads average 30 feet, largest is 39' describes pad length, not what may be parked on it. 2 VEHICLES PER CAMPSITE, and the booking system says NO OVERFLOW PARKING IS AVAILABLE while the brochure prices limited overflow parking at $8/night/vehicle -- a second open conflict, and the one that decides where a third car goes. Maximum 8 people per family site, infants and children included. A maximum of TWO family campsites per household, customer name, primary occupant or registered vehicle on any date; additional sites are cancelled. Hot showers, flush toilets, amphitheatre, seasonal campfire programs and a dump station (additional use fees may apply). Every site has a picnic table and fire ring with grill. Tents must stand on dirt or designated pads, never on lawns; there is no limit on the number. FIRES only in designated areas, only commercially bought wood, processed logs or cut lumber -- COLLECTING WOOD IS PROHIBITED, unlike on the national forest land elsewhere in this dataset -- attended by an adult and fully extinguished on departure. Generators, smoking and vaping are prohibited outright. No camp store. LIMITED TO NO CELL SERVICE and no wifi. Beer and wine only, 21+, at campsites or picnic areas and not in parking lots, on trails or at swim beaches; no hard alcohol. PETS: Ordinance 38 s.801.2(i) governs cats and other animals -- attended, and leashed or contained. The campground's own rules are written for dogs: maximum 3 per site, leashed in developed areas, waste binned, CONFINED TO VEHICLE OR TENT DURING QUIET HOURS, never left unattended, and noisy or uncontrollable dogs asked to leave. Whether the quiet-hours confinement is applied to a cat is not stated by any source read here. Sits about 1.5 miles above Lake Chabot; registered campers park free at the Lake Chabot Marina, and swimming is never permitted there. Campsites are for overnight use only -- meet visitors in the day-use parts of the park. EBRPD gives the park as 3,304 acres on its own page and 5,067 on the booking system, and the drive from downtown Oakland as both 20 and 35 minutes; neither gates a decision, so no conflict was opened for them.

Everything below is still from web-search summaries rather than a page read here. EVIDENCE AGAINST THE RESOLUTION, ARRIVING THE SAME DAY: ReserveAmerica's Coyote Hills listing says 'Dumbarton Quarry and Ardenwood Historic Farm parks are located nearby' -- calling Dumbarton a PARK, and placing it NEARBY rather than inside. But the reading is now 2-2 across sources rather than 2-1, and the caution above about inheriting Coyote Hills' gate and fee matters more for it. THE BALANCE SHIFTED AGAIN ON 2026-09-16, AND THE RESOLUTION IS KEPT ANYWAY. Dumbarton has its OWN ReserveAmerica facility page, EB/110750, separate from Coyote Hills' EB/110453 -- so the booking system that was cited as placing it 'within Coyote Hills Regional Park' also sells it as a facility in its own right, and on Coyote Hills' page calls it a park located nearby. Against the Coyote Hills brochure listing it under that park's Camping heading, the count is now roughly three to one AGAINST. It is kept because a brochure's Camping heading is still the only source making a claim about BOUNDARIES, while a separate booking facility and a park-finder entry are claims about how EBRPD organises its own systems -- Star Mine has a separate entrance too and nobody doubts it is in Black Diamond. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT is Dumbarton's own page on ebparks.org, which has not been read. ONE PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE IS NOW GONE: this row has its own coordinate, at campground precision, off its own facility page, so no search depends on the park field to place it. What still depends on it is the $5 parking and the six seasonal gate bands it inherits from Coyote Hills, and this camp has its own entrance at 9400 Quarry Road, about two miles from Coyote Hills' own point.

name: Round Valley Backpack Camp
notes: Minimum 1, maximum 25 -- a solo camper or a party of twenty-five. A primitive, FENCED site for hike-in, equestrian and bicycle campers, with graded tent pads, a picnic table, an ADA-accessible vault toilet and hitching rails. NO WATER AT THE SITE, and that is the settled reading of three sources that look like they disagree: the park page says non-potable water is available, the booking system says NO WATER and to bring all you need, and EBRPD's alerts page says the supply is not working until further notice. The supply exists, it is non-potable, and it is broken -- so the park page describes the normal state and the booking system the current one. Drinking water IS available at the Marsh Creek staging area, before the walk. THE WALK IS 3.4 OR 3.6 MILES depending which source you read: the booking system gives 18,000 feet, which is 3.41 miles, and the park page says 3.6 from the Marsh Creek Staging Area. Neither gates a decision at that margin, so no conflict thread was opened, but a party carrying every litre of its own water should plan for the longer one. SUMMER HEAT IS THE REAL CONSTRAINT: EBRPD warns temperatures here commonly exceed 100F, and this is a multi-mile carry to a site with no water. 2 vehicles. Parking passes are emailed about a week before and MUST BE PRINTED and displayed on the dash. Haul out all trash. NO DOGS ANYWHERE IN THIS PARK -- see the park-scoped rule; the reason is the endangered San Joaquin kit fox, to which dogs are a disease vector. Pets allowed here are listed as HORSE only. Round Valley is open year round, despite the booking system labelling the loop 'Backpack Seasonal'.

NO vehicle access (driving into/out of site).' So a party of up to fifty carries its kit a quarter mile, and the ten vehicles the listing permits stay at the lot. THE FIRE PIT AGAINST THE REST OF THIS DATASET: EBRPD's backpack sites ban fires outright and Black Diamond bans them park-wide, so a provided pit and a lit fire circle are the exception, and Ordinance 38 s.404's 'only in the facilities provided' is what governs it. name: Corral Group Camp
coord_source: ReserveAmerica's Las Trampas overview page, read 2026-09-16. PARK PRECISION: the pair is on the park overview and matches the park's street address at the end of Bollinger Canyon Road, which is also where the map puts Corral Camp, so it is probably close -- but the page is about the park and the field is labelled accordingly.
nightly_entry_cutoff: Gate hours run in six seasonal bands, 8am to between 5:30pm and 8pm, and MARCH 8 SITS IN TWO BANDS THAT DISAGREE BY AN HOUR -- see the park's access row. No park curfew is published here, unlike four other EBRPD parks in this dataset.
fee_notes: NO NIGHTLY RATE ON FILE -- absent is not free, and the site fee must be confirmed with EBRPD Reservations. A SECURITY DEPOSIT is required: the District's group terms set it at one night's site fee, fully refundable. A GROUP BEER AND WINE PERMIT must be bought in advance if you want either; the only price this project has for it is $25.00, from Arroyo Flats. NO PARK ENTRANCE FEE IS PUBLISHED for Las Trampas at all -- see the park access row, where silence is recorded as silence rather than as free.
notes: THE FIRST DRIVE-IN GROUP CAMP IN THIS DATASET, and it arrives after four days of correcting group camps in the other direction. Sixteen group camps here were hike-in, three of them corrected from a wrong drive_in; this one states 'Site Access: Drive-In' on its own booking page and adds a field nothing else has used -- 'Driveway Entry: Pull-Through'. So the rule that was forming, that EBRPD group camps are walked into, was a fact about the eight parks read first and not about the District. IT IS ALSO AN EQUESTRIAN CAMP: 'Pets Allowed: Domestic, Horse', and the booking category is 'Group Site, Horse Site' -- the same pairing Stewartville carries and the only other one here. EBRPD describes it as 'a primitive group campsite for BOTH EQUESTRIAN AND NON-EQUESTRIAN groups'. MINIMUM 17, MAXIMUM 50, 10 vehicles. SEASONALLY CLOSED 1 NOVEMBER - 31 MARCH, which is a DIFFERENT season from Briones' and Reinhardt Redwood's 1 November - 15 May: five months rather than five and a half, and it reopens six weeks earlier. The booking system's 'Open Through 31 Oct 2026' agrees with it here, where at Reinhardt the same field disagreed with its own page by nine weeks -- so that field coincides with the season sometimes and is still not evidence of one. FACILITIES: five 6ft tables, a serving table, TWO XL BBQs, and two chemical toilets. No water is promised -- see below. 'COWS AND COW PIES MAY BE PRESENT', stated by EBRPD on the listing, which is the plainest sentence in this dataset and matters for a group choosing where to pitch. WHETHER YOU MAY USE THOSE TWO BBQs IS CONTRADICTED ON THE SAME PAGES -- see the las-trampas-bbq thread. The description lists two XL BBQs and the site details flag BBQ: Y. The campground rules on the same listing say 'No campfires/BBQ's. Camp stoves ok.', and the park's own Facilities paragraph says 'NO campfires are permitted' without mentioning barbecues. A group that plans to grill and finds it banned has a different evening. WATER: CAMPERS MUST BRING THEIR OWN, and the park says so three times -- park page, map and booking system. Two faucets exist and neither is promised; EBRPD asks you to contact park staff before your reservation for an update. Recorded in water_sources with a log entry, because this is the first source in this project the agency itself describes as unreliable rather than merely unchecked. BOOKING: phone only, at least 72 hours (3 days) before arrival, maximum 2 reservations per call. Arrival dates July-December 2026 open; January-June 2027 opens December 2026. The map puts Corral Camp near the Bollinger Staging Area at about 500 feet, beside the Little Hills Picnic Ranch and Las Trampas Stables.

name: Morgan Territory Backpack Camp
coord_source: ReserveAmerica's Morgan Territory overview page, read 2026-09-16. PARK PRECISION, and here that matters more than usual: the camp is approximately 4.5 MILES from the parking, so this point is nowhere near it. It answers 'how far is this park from home' and nothing else.
nightly_entry_cutoff: CAMPERS MUST ARRIVE BEFORE POSTED GATE HOURS; gates reopen at 8am daily. Gate hours run in six seasonal bands, 8am to between 5pm and 8pm -- so in January a camper must be through the gate by 5pm and cannot leave before 8am. With parking 4.5 miles out, the walk in has to fit inside that. Roadside parking is highly discouraged.
fee_notes: NO NIGHTLY RATE ON FILE -- absent is not free, and the site fee must be confirmed with EBRPD Reservations. The $8.00 reservation fee paid at booking is non-refundable, and cancelling or changing costs a further $8.00, so a cancelled trip costs $16 before any nightly rate. The park charges nothing for parking.
notes: THE CONSTRUCTED NAME TURNED OUT TO BE THE PUBLISHED ONE. This row was keyed 'Morgan Territory Backpack Camp' yesterday because nothing read named the camp, and the booking system calls it exactly that. That is a convention holding, not a licence to construct names: the flag was right to be there and would have been right if the name had been wrong. PARKING IS APPROXIMATELY 4.5 MILES FROM THE SITE -- the longest carry in this project by a mile, past Stewartville's 3.2 and Wee-Ta-Chi's 1.5, against a quarter mile at Star Mine, Dairy Glen and Arroyo Flats. 'This is a hike-in only site.' 5 parking passes, NO overflow, and the site details say maximum 4 vehicles -- see the morgan-territory-vehicles thread, which is the same defect Stewartville carries. MINIMUM 1, MAXIMUM 20. A solo camper can book it, which is what a backpack site means and is worth holding against the round-valley-camp-class thread: THIS site's 'Looking For Category' reads 'Group Site, Horse Site, Tent Site' while its page heading is BACKPACK SITE and its loop is 'Backpack Seasonal'. So that category field is a multi-valued search facet, not a class -- which is most of the answer to why a neighbouring map could call Round Valley's camp a group camp. CAMPERS ARE RESTRICTED TO THE CAMPSITE DURING CURFEW HOURS, 10pm-5am. That is the sentence this project has been missing: it says a reservation does let you be in the park overnight, and what it costs you is the freedom to move. Mission Peak's page warns of citation or arrest after posted hours with a $300 minimum and says nothing about campers; this park's own hours read 'unless otherwise posted or permitted'. Together they are the clearest answer available, and none of the three sentences is about Mission Peak's camp. SEASONALLY CLOSED 1 NOVEMBER - 1 APRIL, the loop named 'Backpack Seasonal'. A fourth season shape in this District: Briones and Reinhardt Redwood close 1 Nov-15 May, Las Trampas 1 Nov-31 March, this 1 Nov-1 April. FACILITIES: picnic tables, a VAULT TOILET, hitching rails and a horse water trough. NON-POTABLE WATER at the site -- filter, treat, boil or bring your own. No flush toilets and no showers. Pets Allowed: Domestic, Horse -- the third equestrian camp here after Stewartville and Las Trampas' Corral, and a Horse Hitching Post flag. 'DO NOT CAMP UNDER THE TREES, USE OPEN SPACE.' No other camp in this dataset tells you where within the site to pitch. NO CAMPFIRES, camp stoves OK. ALCOHOL NOT PERMITTED, which is the District's backpack rule and not a park quirk. The camp is on Roger Epperson Ridge between the Clyma and Highland Ridge Trails; Stone Corral Trail is closed at a Highland Ridge junction and whether that affects the route is still unstated.

name: Wild Turkey Group Camp
coord_source: No coordinate. Del Valle's park point belongs to the family campground and these sit apart from it; nothing read gives them one of their own.
nightly_entry_cutoff: Del Valle's gate hours are disputed, 9pm or 10pm -- see the del-valle-gate-close thread and the park's access row. ReserveAmerica adds that GROUP campsite gate hours change seasonally and publishes no bands, which is the sentence that revealed these camps existed.
notes: NAMED ON THE OHLONE WILDERNESS PERMIT MAP AND NOWHERE ELSE THIS PROJECT HAS READ. Two days ago ReserveAmerica's Del Valle page said 'Group campsite gate hours change seasonally' and this project held no group campsite at Del Valle at all, which was logged as a gap. This map closes it by naming five: Wild Turkey Group Camp, Punta Vaca Group Camp, Cedar Group Camp, Lil Chaparral Horse Camp and Caballo Loco Horse Camp, clustered near the Del Valle Family Campground at the north end of the Ohlone Trail. THE TYPE IS IN THE NAME, WHICH IS WHY THESE ARE ADDED WHERE REINHARDT'S EIGHT LABELS WERE NOT. There the map distinguished Reservable Group Camp from Reservable Picnic Area by symbol and the flattened PDF lost the symbols, so guessing would have been wrong five times in eight. Here each label says Group Camp or Horse Camp in words. EVERYTHING ELSE IS UNKNOWN AND LEFT BLANK. ACCESS MODE IS NOT RECORDED -- the map names the camp and says nothing about whether you drive to it, and after four access corrections in five days nothing is written without a source. Nor is there a capacity, a minimum party size, a fee, no water, no restroom, no season, no check-in. Del Valle is the oldest EBRPD park in this dataset, added before any per-park reading began, and the one park whose campground list has never been checked against a ReserveAmerica campsites page. That page would fill all of this at once. On the Vallecitos Trail side of the cluster.
